title: Influence of Insertion Angle on the Ultrasound Visibility of Flow-Switch Arterial Catheters: An Investigation in Phantom and Cadaver Models
summary:
This study investigates the ultrasound visibility of various catheters with so-called flow-switch technology as well as standard peripheral intravenous cannulas when inserted into different media—an artificial gel phantom and human tissue (cadaveric specimens). Three insertion angles (20°, 30°, and 40°) are examined, and a total of seven different needle types are compared.

The aim of the study is to determine under which conditions needles are particularly well or poorly visualized on ultrasound. This is of particular relevance for medical education, as ultrasound-guided puncture techniques are typically learned and practiced in simulation before being applied in clinical patient care. The direct comparison with human tissue is intended to assess how well the simulation models reflect realistic conditions and to identify which combinations of needle type, insertion angle, and medium are most suitable for training purposes.

The results of this study are expected to contribute to more practice-oriented and effective training, with the ultimate goal of improving the safety and success of ultrasound-guided invasive procedures.
